newsitem.title: USA: Stocks skid anew on interest-rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Stocks skid anew on interest-rate jitters.

text.p: The stock market was sent reeling Monday, picking up where it left off last week, as Wall Street fretted about the jump in interest rates.

At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 99.71 points at 6,640.88 following a mid-morning plunge of more than 141 points, which came on the heels of Thursday's 140-point fall. Financial markets were closed for Good Friday.
In the broader market, declining issues swamped advances 5-1 on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 291 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 21.69 points at 1,227.82.

The drop came after new data that showed the economy was still in high gear, which heightened the risk of more monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve in the months ahead. Last week, the Fed announced a quarter-point increase in short-term interest rates, in an effort to keep the economy from over-heating.

The goverment reported that February personal income rose a higher-than-forecast 0.9 percent vs. a revised 0.4 percent increase the previous month, while consumption rose a smaller-than-expected 0.3 percent, compared with a revised 0.1 percent gain in January.
The data showed that the economy was expanding at a brisk pace.
In the bond market, the key 30-year Treasury bond lost 4/32, and its yield rose to 7.10 percent from Thursday's close of 7.09 percent.

The 7 percent yield on the long bond will likely draw investors away from stocks into bonds. Analysts said a move above 7.20 percent would mean an even more serious psycholgical and technical breakdown for stocks.
Analysts said the market might come under further fire Tuesday when European investors return from the long Easter holiday weekend.
Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said the Dow ran into support at the 6,600 level.

"But it was purely a technical bounce. There are too many questions worrying the market. Above all, the consensus is shifting in favour of the Fed raising rates one or two more times," he said. "It means you have competition for the investment dollar from the debt market."
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co., said corporate earnings were another big worry for investors.
"As the quarter begins, there will be a lot more concern that earnings will disappoint," he said.

"I think the market is in a difficult position in which the economy will do very well, interest rates will edge up and earnings will not follow suit," Metz said. "The question lurking in the background is what will those people who have been throwing money at index funds do."
Metz said, "They may panic at the wrong time and sell, but I think the market has to go a bit lower before we test the stamina of the mutual fund buyer."
Among special situations, Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. was down 5-3/8 at 32-3/8 after Goldman Sachs cut its rating on the stock.

The most actively traded Nasdaq issue was Ascend Communications Inc., down 10-3/4 at 41-1/4, followed by Cascade Communications Corp., off 1-5/16 at 27-1/16. Ascend announced a $3.7 billion agreement to acquire Cascade.
Shiva Corp. sank 3-1/4 to 8-5/8 after the company said its first quarter earnings and revenues would be below analysts' expectations.
